title: A new prediction model for acute kidney injury following liver transplantation using grafts from donors after cardiac death.
summary: A gradient-boosting model for acute kidney injury after liver transplantation using donation-after-circulatory-death grafts achieved AUC 0.75 in a later temporal cohort of 195 recipients. The retrospective, single-center evaluation had no external validation.
ai_technology: A gradient-boosting model used clinical features to predict acute kidney injury after liver transplantation with DCD grafts.
organization: Department of Critical Care Medicine, Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, China; Department of the Forth Wards of Liver Disease, Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, China; Department of Liver Transplantation Center, Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, China; Department of Medical Oncology, Beijing Youan Hospital, Capital Medical University, China

evidence.tested: In the later temporal cohort, the model reported AUC 0.75 (95% CI 0.67–0.81), F1 0.72, sensitivity 0.73 and specificity 0.63.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective single-center study: 894 recipients in model development and a later 195-recipient cohort from the same hospital. No external validation was reported.
evidence.ai_role: The learned model estimated post-transplant AKI risk and was evaluated in a later cohort from the same center.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results in Europe PMC/PMC and publisher publication record.
